title: Perf-canary: add mixed-length burst scenario to induce KV fragmentation + measure p95/p99 sensitivity
creator: Marcus Reed
description:
We need a perf-canary scenario that reliably reproduces the fragmentation patterns we see in production (mixed sequence lengths + churn + bursts), and that is sensitive to p95/p99 regressions introduced by KV cache compaction/eviction changes.

This ticket adds a new perf-canary scenario (and thresholds/alerts) designed to:
- Drive allocator fragmentation upward in a repeatable way.
- Exercise scheduler boundaries (prefill/decode) with burst arrivals.
- Surface decode tail spikes (p95/p99) correlated with compaction/eviction work.

Outcome: perf-canary will block regressions for runtime-1.22 compaction rollout and provide an always-on early warning if compaction budgets/thresholds are too aggressive (latency spikes) or too lax (fragmentation/evictions/OOM risk).
acceptance_criteria:
- Scenario is reproducible across 3 consecutive runs (fragmentation curve + latency quantiles within agreed variance bands).
- Scenario induces fragmentation ratio above trigger threshold (target: >= 0.25 steady / >= 0.35 peak) when compaction is disabled or budget=0.
- With compaction enabled (default canary settings), scenario shows:
  - No >10% regression in throughput vs baseline scenario set.
  - p99 decode latency does not regress >8% vs control build for same GPU/model.
  - Compaction work is visible in telemetry (bytes moved, compaction time) without causing sustained scheduler stalls.
- Alerts/thresholds added and routed to #eng-sre + #eng-runtime for canary failures.
- Documentation added to perf-canary scenario README (what it tests, how to interpret failures, how to rerun locally).
scenario_spec:
Name: kv_fragmentation_mixed_length_bursts

High-level shape:
- Warmup: 3 minutes steady arrivals, moderate concurrency, mixed prompt lengths.
- Burst phase: 30s on / 90s off bursts for 12 minutes total; burst arrival rate is 4–6x steady.
- Churn: during burst phase, 20–30% of requests are canceled mid-decode (to exercise relocation + cancellation edge cases).
- Long-lived sessions: maintain a background set of N “sticky” sessions (pinned) that continue decoding across the entire run to simulate long chat sessions that anchor KV allocations.

Traffic distribution:
- Prompt lengths (prefill tokens): mixture model (e.g., 20% @ 128, 35% @ 512, 30% @ 2k, 15% @ 4k).
- Output lengths (decode tokens): heavy tail (median ~256, p95 ~1.5k).
- Concurrency targets: steady=24 in-flight, burst=96 in-flight (cap with backpressure to avoid pure overload artifacts).

Runtime knobs:
- Run variant A (control): compaction disabled (or budget=0), eviction policy disabled.
- Run variant B (treatment): compaction enabled with canary budget defaults + eviction policy enabled for low-priority tier only.

Measured signals (required):
- p50/p95/p99 end-to-end latency, plus decode-only p95/p99.
- Tokens/sec throughput (prefill+decode separated if available).
- KV fragmentation ratio (allocator metric) over time.
- Compaction bytes moved + time spent (per interval), eviction counters.
- OOM / request shedding counts (should remain 0 in canary; if non-zero, scenario parameters need tuning).
thresholds_and_alerting:
Initial pass/fail thresholds (subject to tuning during first week):
- p99_decode_ms: fail if > (baseline_mean + 8%) or > baseline_mean + 25ms (whichever is larger) for 2 consecutive windows.
- fragmentation_ratio_peak: warn if <0.30 in control variant (means scenario no longer inducing fragmentation and loses signal).
- compaction_time_budget_overrun: warn if compaction_time_ms exceeds budget by >2x in 3+ consecutive windows (indicates scheduler hook failure or runaway compaction).
- eviction_rate: warn if eviction_count/min exceeds expected band under treatment variant (helps detect too-aggressive eviction causing churn).

Routing:
- Failures page #eng-sre oncall (tail latency regression) and tag #eng-runtime for compaction-specific failures.
- Include run link + dashboards + exemplar trace IDs if available.
implementation_notes:
Implementation work lives in perf-canary repo; scenario generator borrowed patterns from the new workload generator in benchmark-lab (mixed length + churn).

Key tasks:
1) Add scenario definition + parameters (burst cadence, distributions, cancelation behavior, sticky sessions).
2) Ensure scenario captures allocator metrics (fragmentation ratio) and compaction metrics from runtime exports.
3) Add comparison mode: control vs treatment build (or feature-flag toggled) so we can detect regressions due to compaction.
4) Add baseline recording and tolerances; verify flake rate is acceptable (target <5% false positives).

Notes:
- Avoid turning this into a pure overload test; we want fragmentation + compaction sensitivity, not queueing collapse.
- Use backpressure caps so decode tail reflects allocator/compaction work rather than admission control artifacts.
- Cancellation behavior must be representative but not so high that it dominates latency with cancellation bookkeeping.
comments: 2026-01-09 — Allison Grant (Observability): Please ensure the scenario emits/records kv_fragmentation_ratio and compaction_bytes_moved in the same timebase as latency quantiles so dashboards can correlate. If perf-canary can attach exemplar trace IDs for spikes, even better.

2026-01-10 — Sean Gallagher (SRE): +1. Also please route failures to #eng-sre with a clear label (tail-latency regression vs fragmentation-signal lost). We’ve had canaries fail in ways that were hard to triage quickly.

2026-01-14 — Sofia Ivanova (Scheduler): Make sure burst cadence crosses prefill/decode boundaries; we specifically saw issues when compaction work landed on decode hot paths. If you can split decode-only p99, that’ll help isolate scheduler effects.

2026-01-20 — Rina Kobayashi: Draft scenario parameters posted in PR. Early runs show control variant peak fragmentation ~0.38 on H100, treatment ~0.21 with compaction budget=2ms/step. However p99 decode variance is a bit high run-to-run; tuning cancelation rate down from 35% to 25%.

2026-01-23 — Marcus Reed: Reviewed. Please keep sticky sessions; that’s the closest proxy we have to long-lived chat allocations. Also can we cap max output tokens for the heavy-tail bucket so we don’t create a handful of extreme outliers that dominate p99?

2026-01-27 — Sahana Iyer (CI/perf reliability): We should gate this scenario to nightly + runtime-PR label initially. Running control+treatment on every perf-canary invocation will increase total time. Can we start with treatment-only on PRs and do A/B nightly?

2026-02-03 — Rina Kobayashi: Implemented treatment-only on PR runs; control+treatment A/B nightly. Added explicit check that control still produces fragmentation peak >=0.30 (otherwise we page the scenario owner to retune).

2026-02-10 — Sean Gallagher: Thresholds look reasonable. Please ensure the failure output includes the compaction bytes moved/time series summary so oncall can quickly tell if it’s a compaction runaway vs general perf regression.
2026-02-12 — Connor O’Brien (Release): Marking as done once PR merges + dashboards updated under ENG-4830. This is a runtime-1.22 rollout gate.
